title: A Mixtape for the Group Chat
premise: August Underhill has spent seventeen years perfecting invisibility in the small town of Halloway, until a college essay prompt—'Describe a moment you couldn't stay silent'—cracks them open. The essay they write names what really happened last spring: how their best friend Dex's older brother died in a 'freak accident' at the quarry that August knows was something else, and how the whole town, including August, agreed to look away. When the draft accidentally gets shared to the group chat by a well-meaning friend, August's carefully managed life detonates: Dex stops speaking to them, the sheriff's office takes sudden interest, and the victim's mother finally asks August directly for the truth. In the end, August reads the essay aloud at the school board meeting, trading their quiet future in Halloway for justice—and discovers that telling the truth didn't cost them their found family; it was the price of actually having one.
about_author: Yara Coldharbour grew up in a mill town of fewer than a thousand people and writes about the teenagers who survive them. They live with two cats and an ever-growing archive of unsent group chat messages.

chapters.title: Prompt Number Four
chapters.summary: August's POV. Assigned a college essay over winter break, August drafts safe answers about volunteering and cross-country—until prompt four ('a moment you couldn't stay silent') drags up the night at the quarry last spring. They write the true version at 2 a.m., save it as 'DO NOT SEND,' and tell themselves it's just practice. The emotional beat is dread disguised as relief: the truth exists now, outside their body.

chapters.title: Sent
chapters.summary: August's POV, shifting to group-chat transcripts. Best friend Priya, trying to help, uploads August's essay folder to the chat meant for shared study notes. The message sits unread for six hours, then detonates: Dex replies with one word—'wow'—and leaves the chat. The sheriff calls August's mom. The beat is vertigo; August watches their silence get read aloud by everyone at once.

chapters.title: What the Quarry Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating August and Priya POVs. Mrs. Okafor, the dead boy's mother, asks August to meet; she's known for a year that the official story was wrong but needed someone else to say it first. Meanwhile Dex confronts August—not denying the truth, but furious that August let him grieve a lie while staying safe. The beat is the cost of honesty made flesh: August loses the friendship precisely because they were right.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the school board meeting convened to 'address rumors,' August stands and reads the essay from the top instead of apologizing. Half the room walks out; Mrs. Okafor doesn't. Afterward, Dex appears in the parking lot holding his brother's old mixtape—the one labeled for August—and presses play on the car stereo. The beat is resolution without repair: justice begins, the family re-forms around the truth, and August submits the essay unchanged.
